newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power extends gain on cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power extends gain on cold.

text.p: Outlook of a weekend cold front moving in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic pushed up the region's spot bulk electricity prices for a second day.
"It's totally weather driven," said a Northeast trader.
The weather system moving from the Midwest was forecast to bring 40s-50s Fahrenheit temperatures to the area, compared with current levels in the 60s-70s range.
Support from cooler weather was offset by more generation capacity returning to service from recent shutdowns.
The 1,031 megawatt (MW) Hope Creek nuclear plant in Salem, N.J., was in startup mode after being shut last Saturday than a week ago for maintenance.
The 610 MW Oyster Creek nuclear power plant in Forked River, N.J., was running at 80 percent of capacity following its autumn refueling outage.

The 1,090 MW Susquehanna 1 nuclear power unit in Berwick, Pa., continued to hold at 75 percent power amid work on a reactor feed pump. The unit was shut Oct 28 to replace a section of a steam drain pipe.
"There's enough generation there," a PJM marketer said.

Swing domestic natural gas prices were firm on the expected cold weather from the Midwest through the eastern seaboard. Spot natgas for this weekend through Monday at Philadelphia's city gate was offered as high as $3.40 per million British thermal units.
Power scheduling into eastern PJM from the western district remained restricted due to the reduced operation at the Whitpain substation, north of Philadelphia.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Saturday was quoted near $22.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), for Sunday $21.50, for Monday $25.00-$26.00 and for Tuesday $25.00-$25.50.
Trades of Monday PJM power were heard done at $25.50-$25.90. Today's quotes compared with Thursday's $23.50-$24.50 for Friday delivery.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Monday delivery held steady against Thursday's $14.00-$15.00 for Friday delivery.
December PJM electricity for firm delivery during heavy load hours were discussed between $28.10 and $28.30, compared with Thursday's $28.15-$28.30.
January/February 1997 PJM deliveries were valued at $32.10-$32.50, a wider range than Thursday's $32.15-$32.30.
March 1997 PJM electricity was pegged at $24.00-$24.60, down from Thursday's $24.50-$24.80.
Brokers and marketers said spot PJM prices will decline when the cold weather moderates by the middle of next week.
